title: rollout-controller: treat stale/unavailable SLO monitors as UNKNOWN (guardrail against false rollbacks)
author: Benji Okafor
description:
Context: During staged enablement of auto-rollback, we observed a small number of rollbacks that were later attributed to missing/stale monitor data (monitor query timed out / last datapoint lagging). In the current evaluator pipeline, some error paths end up looking like a breach because we fall back to conservative defaults without distinguishing "no data" from "bad data". This PR adds an explicit UNKNOWN health verdict and a guardrail so we do not auto-rollback when the required SLO monitors are stale or unavailable.

What changes: (1) Introduce a third verdict state: UNKNOWN (in addition to HEALTHY/UNHEALTHY). UNKNOWN is returned when monitor fetch fails, monitor query returns no series, or the newest sample timestamp is older than max_staleness. (2) Gate rollback executor: only trigger auto-rollback when verdict == UNHEALTHY. UNKNOWN will emit audit+events but will not change traffic split. (3) Add explicit "reason" and "evidence" fields to decision trace logging to make dashboards and oncall triage clearer (e.g., stale_monitor, fetch_timeout, empty_result). (4) Add internal metrics/counters for UNKNOWN verdicts and stale monitor occurrences to support alert tuning.

Policy semantics: The global behavior remains consistent with ADR direction (do not take irreversible action on missing signals). This PR defaults evaluator to fail-open for rollback (i.e., UNKNOWN => no rollback). The oncall signal is still preserved via alerting on elevated UNKNOWN rates and via event stream notifications so we can respond to monitoring outages.

Defaults: max_staleness defaults to 6m (covers scrape + query delay for the rollout SLO templates) and can be overridden per environment. Minimum traffic guardrails remain unchanged.

Why hotfix-style: SUP-18457 escalation asked for immediate mitigation before we expand the staged cohort. This change reduces rollback flapping caused by monitoring gaps without changing breach thresholds.

Test plan: unit tests for verdict computation with stale timestamps / empty series / fetch errors; integration-style test in simulator to ensure UNKNOWN does not invoke executor; manual: induced monitor API timeout in dev and verified console shows UNKNOWN verdict with reason and no traffic revert.

Follow-ups: console UX copy for UNKNOWN (work in ENG-2316) and alert threshold tuning for UNKNOWN rate (ENG-2318).
commits: rollout-controller: add UNKNOWN verdict type + reason codes
slo-monitor client: surface sample timestamps and last-successful-fetch time
executor: require UNHEALTHY verdict for rollback action
tests: cover fetch-timeout/empty result/stale datapoint scenarios
conversation:
Nadia Rahman: Can we distinguish monitor fetch failure vs empty result? Empty result sometimes indicates label mismatch (migration) rather than outage. Also please add a metric so observability can alert on this.

Benji Okafor: Yep. Added reason codes: fetch_error, timeout, empty_result, stale_sample. Also added unknown_verdict_total labeled by reason + monitor_type and stale_monitor_total for staleness specifically. Will coordinate with ENG-2322 for label migration to reduce empty_result.

---
Miles Thornton: The default max_staleness=6m seems okay, but can we document why and ensure it’s configurable? Also: executor should be explicit that UNKNOWN never rolls back; don’t rely on caller behavior.

Benji Okafor: Added max_staleness to defaults with env override and a comment referencing scrape/query latency. Updated executor to require verdict==UNHEALTHY (and log when verdict==UNKNOWN).

---
Sean Gallagher: +1 on fail-open for rollback. Please ensure oncall still gets a signal when UNKNOWN is spiking; otherwise we’ll silently lose protection.

Benji Okafor: Added event emission for UNKNOWN (severity=warning) with links to dashboards/runbook, and metrics for alerting. No traffic changes.

---
Jada Williams: Small nit: decision trace currently only stores "healthy/unhealthy" string; console will need to display UNKNOWN. Can we keep the wire format stable?

Benji Okafor: Kept existing fields and added verdict_enum + verdict_reason as additive fields. Old consumers keep working; new consumers can switch to enum.

---
Miles Thornton: Approved after the executor guard and metrics landed.

Nadia Rahman: Approved. Please ping me when the UNKNOWN alert is added to the dashboard pack.

Sean Gallagher: Approved. This unblocks cohort expansion.
release_notes: Auto-rollback now treats stale/unavailable SLO monitor data as UNKNOWN and will not rollback on missing signals; added visibility via metrics and decision trace reasons.
